name: Hollin Barrow
formed_by_story: Cut into chalk as a Vale barrow, roofed with flint and turf. Two hundred years later a yew took root on the mound and its roots came down through the roof, breaking the chambers open into one another and letting the rain in.
who_was_here: The Hollin families buried their reeves here with their tools, and stopped when the reeves would not stay buried.
story: A working man's grave. The Barrow Reeve was buried with his bell-hammer, the one he rang to call the harvest in, and he has been calling ever since to a village that no longer answers. Everything in here is a farm tool, and everything in here is still being used.
unique_object: the Reeve's bell-hammer, a hay-mallet with a hand-bell cast into its head

beats.note: A turf-roofed porch between two flint uprights. Daylight reaches four metres and stops.
Chalk steps worn into a ramp. A yew root has split them down the middle.
The first burial chamber. The roof fell here when the yew came through; rain has made a chalk paste of the floor.
A corridor the roots have narrowed to a squeeze. You go sideways.
A long chamber where the reeves' tools were stacked for the next harvest. Somebody has been sharpening them.
The low point. Rain has been collecting here for a century; the chalk has gone milky.
A gap between two fallen roof slabs. A tall man would think twice.
A side cist nobody disturbed, because a small bell hangs in its doorway and the wights will not pass it.
The reeve's own chamber, pillared with chalk and flint. Four cists in the walls, all open. The shaft above was the yew's doing.
A spoil shaft the diggers used, climbing back toward the porch. Barred from the far side until somebody lifts the bar.

shortcut.note: The bar lifts only from the barrow side, so the way back opens once, and stays open.

encounters.note: One wight standing in the light shaft, not moving. It is holding a scythe and facing the wall.
Two at the tool racks, one above on the ledge who drops in behind you when the first is struck.
Standing in the water up to the knee. The water slows your dodge; theirs is slower.

features.name: Bell Cist
features.note: The hanging bell is why this cist is safe, and why it is the only warm thing down here.
A scythe leaning where a man would leave it, sharpened this week.
Open, and the lid is on the floor face down, which is how you lay a lid you mean to put back.
